newsitem.title: ITALY: Alitalia close to deal with Alpi Eagles -- report.
newsitem.headline: Alitalia close to deal with Alpi Eagles -- report.

text.p: Italian state airline Alitalia is close to reaching a deal to sublease five Fokker airliners and hand over several of its national and international routes to private carrier Alpi Eagles, an Italian newspaper reported.

Milan financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore reported on Sunday that the two airlines were expected to sign the agreement under which Alpi Eagles, which started business in June, would take over Alitalia's Fokker 70s and fly them with its own livery.
The five Fokker planes were originally leased by the loss-making state carrier in 1995 as part of former Managing Director Roberto Schisano's policy of developing European regional routes.

Il Sole said Alitalia may take a 20 percent stake in the private airline which is owned by a group of Northeast Italian investors, among them white goods producer Zanussi -- owned by Sweden's Electrolux -- clothes producer Stefanel and the Marzotto textiles group.

Alpi, whose staff costs are reported to be 40 to 50 percent lower than Alitalia's, already operates a fleet of four Fokker 100 airliners using the same Roll-Royce Tay 620 engines which power Alitalia's Fokker 70s.

Alpi would take over Alitalia's regional routes between Venice and Madrid and Barcelona while the two airlines would have a code-sharing arrangement on a new route between Verona in the northeast and the Sicilian city of Catania.

Il Sole also reported that Alitalia was planning to concentrate its medium and long-range routes in Avianova, a subsidiary which at present operates the fleet of Fokkers to be handed over to Alpi Eagles and 13 turbo-prop planes.

Avianova, with significantly lower staff costs than its parent company, would be renamed Alitalia Team and will take over 13 Airbus 321s and six Boeing 767s at the end of the month under the plan, the newspaper reported.
